how.title: Three steps
how.step2Title: Pick a thing to carry it
how.step1Body: Random, or the one you want. The number is yours for life — lose the card and the replacement carries the same number.
how.step2Body: Card, ring, band, windscreen tag, pet tag. One or several — all of them answer to the same number.
how.step3Body: They hold their phone to it and your profile opens. One press saves your contact. You get a record of it — who, when, where.

devices.chip: NTAG213, 144 bytes — enough for the link and nothing spare
devices.battery: No battery. Nothing to charge, nothing to replace
devices.app: No app to install — not for you, not for whoever taps it

card.name: Card
card.tagline: Earns its place in the wallet
card.body: Bank-card size, 0.8 mm thick. Matte black PVC — it does not hold fingerprints and does not scuff in a pocket. The name and number are laser-engraved rather than printed: ink wears off, an engraving does not. Nobody hands this one back out of politeness.

ring.name: Ring
ring.tagline: You shake a hand, the profile opens
ring.body: Ceramic over stainless steel. The tap happens inside the handshake, so there is no separate gesture — and that is the end of looking for a wallet. We send a sizing strip before the order: paper, five minutes. Guess wrong and we exchange it once, free.
ring.spec3: Stays on in water, stays out of the way in the gym

band.name: Band
band.tagline: Lives on the wrist, works on the wrist
band.body: Italian leather, steel magnetic clasp. Wears under a watch or instead of one. Sweat and rain are fine; the leather darkens over time, which is not a fault — that is how leather ages. You cut it to length yourself, and the ruler is in the box.
band.spec3: Holds up to sweat and rain

cartag.name: Car tag
cartag.tagline: Behind the windscreen, instead of your number
cartag.body: A black plate that sits under the glass. Instead of a phone number on display for everyone: whoever taps it writes or calls, and never sees the number. Parked somewhere awkward, that person reaches you directly — before anyone calls a tow truck.
cartag.spec2: Does not fade in sun or crack in frost

pettag.name: Pet tag
pettag.tagline: If they wander off, whoever finds them taps
pettag.body: A light tag for the collar. Whoever finds them taps a phone and sees your name, your number and a note about medication. No app — which is exactly why it works: the finder installs nothing. Change the details whenever you like; the tag stays the same tag.
pettag.spec1: 28 mm, 6 g — light enough for a small dog
pettag.spec2: Steel clip, will not work loose off the collar
pettag.spec3: Rain and swimming pools are fine

stand.name: Stand
stand.tagline: Sits on the table, the guest taps it themselves
stand.body: For a cafe, a salon, a reception desk. It sits on the table: menu, review, Telegram channel — where it leads is your call. NFC on one face and a QR on the other, because not every phone has NFC switched on. It has weight, so it stays put when a sleeve catches it.
stand.spec1: NFC on one face, QR on the other
stand.spec3: Change the link whenever you like

faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: What is a number and how is it priced?
faq.q2: How does the NFC device work?
faq.q3: What does it do for a cafe or a hotel?
faq.q4: How many staff can I add?
faq.a1: A number is a unique code of three letters and three digits — MYN042, say — and it becomes the address of your profile. The price starts from a base and rises with how rare the letters and digits are. Type any combination on the pricing page and its price appears straight away.
faq.a2: Hold the device — card, ring or bracelet — to somebody's phone and your Flex profile opens by itself. Nobody installs an app. Phones without NFC use the QR code instead.
faq.a3: Every table or room gets its own QR code and its own NFC tag. A guest taps it, the menu or service list opens, and from there they call a waiter, ask for the bill or leave a review. The request arrives on the phone by the till with a sound and with the table number on it. The monthly report shows the average time to answer and which table calls most.
faq.a4: The team plan is sold by the seat, minimum five. A seat belongs to the company rather than to a person: when somebody leaves it frees up and goes to the next hire.
faq.a5: Payme for a number and a personal subscription. Cafes, hotels and companies pay by invoice and bank transfer: the document is issued in the cabinet and the subscription is extended when the money arrives.

personal.metaDescription: Three letters and three digits — bought once and yours for life. Engraved on a card, a ring or a band; a tap opens your profile.
personal.titleA: You buy the number once and it stays yours —
personal.lead: This is not a subscription to a number. You buy it and you keep it: lose the card and the replacement carries the same number. Card, ring, band — whichever you take, they all open one profile.
personal.heroPhotoAlt: A Flex card held against a phone
personal.pickLead: Three letters of your name, your company, or simply the three you like. If it is free you see the price here; if it is taken you see who has it.
personal.formulaTitle: How the price is worked out
personal.formula: {base} × how rare the letters are × how rare the digits are
personal.rule1: Words people know cost more: VIP, CEO, OSH, UZB.
personal.rule2: So do three of the same letter or digit: AAA, 777.
personal.rule3: Runs and mirrors cost more than plain digits: 123, 121.
personal.blockedNote: Some combinations are not for sale at all — the abbreviations of state bodies, and words used as insults.
personal.priceLead: Three parts, because they are three different things: the number is scarce, the object is manufactured, and the profile runs every month.
personal.numberNote: Priced by how rare it is. You pay once — there is nothing to renew and no monthly charge on it.
personal.deviceNote: Card, ring, band, windscreen tag, pet tag. Take one or take five — all of them answer to the same number.
personal.planNote: Keeping your page up is free. The monthly part pays for statistics, the contacts you collect, and links without a limit.
personal.plansTitle: What the monthly part is for
personal.plansLead: The profile runs every day: a server, a domain, backups. So there is a free half and a paid half — and the number is yours on both.
personal.freeNote: Included in the price of the number
personal.free1: Your profile page and a QR code
personal.premiumNote: For the profile working in full
personal.premiumYear: {yearly} so'm a year — two months free
personal.prem2: Day-by-day statistics — which link, and where from
personal.prem3: The contacts you collect, exported to Excel
personal.prem4: Your own background picture and the gold trim
personal.prem5: The Flex line comes off the page
personal.lapse: Stop paying and the profile does not go dark — it falls back to the standard plan. The number is yours either way.
personal.arrivesLead: The object and the profile arrive together: open the box, tap it, it works.
personal.arrive1Title: The object, engraved with your number
personal.arrive1Body: Your name and number are cut in with a laser rather than printed on top: ink wears off, an engraving does not.
personal.arrive2Body: That is where the profile lives. A link sent in a message and a tap on the object open the same page.
personal.arrive3Title: A QR code on the back
personal.arrive3Body: For phones without NFC, or with it switched off. Whoever taps it installs nothing.
personal.arrive4Body: Links, services, photograph — you change them yourself. The object stays the object; what is behind it is what changes.
personal.delivery: We deliver across Tashkent. Payment through Payme.
personal.arrivesPhotoAlt: A card, a ring and a band on one table
personal.q1: What if my phone has no NFC?
personal.a1: The QR code on the back works — the camera opens it. On an iPhone NFC is on by itself; on Android it is switched on in the settings.
personal.q2: If I lose the card, do I lose the number?
personal.a2: No. The number belongs to your account, not to the object. Order a new one and it is engraved with the same number; switch the lost one off in the cabinet and it stops working.
personal.q3: What happens if I stop paying monthly?
personal.a3: The profile stays up, it just returns to the standard plan: five links, overall statistics. The number stays yours and is never sold to anybody else.
personal.q4: Will everybody see my phone number?
personal.a4: You decide what stands on the profile. You can hide the phone number and leave only a message or Telegram button — that is exactly how the windscreen tag is meant to work.
personal.q5: Can I move to a different number later?
personal.a5: You can buy another one, but it is another number: the first stays yours as well. So take your time — check it first, then order.
personal.orderLead: Pick the number, pick the object, pay. We do the rest.
personal.orderStep1Body: While the payment is pending, that number is sold to nobody else.
personal.orderStep2Body: Card, ring, band, or several at once. The name and number are engraved.
personal.orderStep3Body: Through Payme. Once it clears, the number is transferred to you and the object goes into production.
personal.orderNote: The order is completed in the cabinet.

pricingPage.metaDescription: How a number's price is worked out, what the devices cost, what the monthly subscription buys and what happens if it lapses.
pricingPage.title: Pricing
pricingPage.lead: Everything is on this page: how a number's price is worked out, what a device costs, what the monthly subscription buys and what happens if the payments stop. Nobody has to be phoned to find out.
pricingPage.ruleTitle: The shape of the number sets the price
pricingPage.ruleBody: Every number is three letters and three digits: ABC123. The base price is the same for everyone. After that it is shape: the rarer the letters, the larger the multiplier, and the same again for the digits. Nothing else is added — which is why you can work out any number's price yourself.
pricingPage.formula: Base price × letter multiplier × digit multiplier
pricingPage.lettersBody: The list holds {rare} words people know, {top} of them status words — VIP, CEO, UZB and the like. Anything not on the list is judged on shape alone.
pricingPage.digitsBody: There is no list on this side, only shape. 777 is three of the same digit, 123 runs in order, 121 is a palindrome, 007 has two leading zeros.
pricingPage.tiersBody: Once the two multipliers are multiplied together, a number lands in one of five tiers. The tier does not change the price — it follows from it.
pricingPage.tierRareNote: One weak pattern on one side — a palindrome or something like it.
pricingPage.tierEpicNote: A strong pattern on one side: a word people know, or digits in a row.
pricingPage.tierLegendaryNote: A strong pattern on both sides.
pricingPage.tierGenesisNote: Both sides at their strongest. Very few are left.
pricingPage.examplesBody: The prices below are calculated from that same formula when the page is rendered — none of them is typed in by hand.
pricingPage.blockedTitle: Combinations that are not for sale
pricingPage.blockedBody: Some letter combinations are not sold at any price: the abbreviations of state bodies, obscenities and sacred names. Such a number looks in the search exactly like a number that does not exist, and it cannot be taken.
pricingPage.devicesBody: The device is paid for separately. A number is expensive because it is scarce; a device is expensive because it was manufactured. Fold them into one price and the owner of a rare number would be paying more for the same piece of steel.
pricingPage.subTitle: What the monthly payment is for
pricingPage.subBody: The number is bought once and stays yours. The subscription is for the profile being open every day, the statistics being collected and the contacts being kept. They are paid for separately because they are separate things: a number is issued once, a server costs money every month.
pricingPage.planFreeNote: Works from the day you take the number. Nothing more to pay.
pricingPage.planPremiumNote: Turns the profile from a display into something you work with.
planPremiumItems: Full analytics — by day and by link
Contacts collected, and an Excel export
The Flex mark is removed from the page
pricingPage.planYearly: A year up front is {price} so'm — twelve months for the price of {months}.
pricingPage.teamBody: Numbers bought for staff are {price} so'm a month per seat, {min} seats minimum. One invoice, one payment. Somebody leaves and the number stays with the company.
pricingPage.venueBody: A venue pays by how many points it has. A point is a table, a room, a door or a chair. The menu, the call button, the QR and the NFC are in the price.
pricingPage.lapsedBody: Everybody asks this one silently, so the answer stands here.
lapsedItems: The profile still opens — a tap on the card brings up the same page.
Editing closes: the profile falls back to the ordinary plan.
The number stays yours and nothing is deleted.
The day the payment resumes, everything is where it was.
pricingPage.ctaBody: Three letters, three digits. It says whether it is free and what it costs.

terms.metaDescription: The rules for using a Flex handle and profile: subscription, passing a handle on, combinations that are not sold, and what the profile's owner answers for.
terms.title: Terms of use
terms.lead: This page sets out the rules for using a Flex handle and profile. The terms of sale — price, payment, delivery and returns — are in a separate document, the public offer. In short: the handle stays yours, the profile keeps opening without a subscription, and what stands on the profile is yours to decide and yours to answer for.
terms.authority: The original of this document is drawn up in Uzbek. The Russian and English versions are provided for convenience; in the event of a discrepancy the Uzbek text governs.
terms.s1p1: These terms cover the use of the service {company} provides: the handle, the profile and the devices that carry them. Using the site and the profile counts as agreement to them.
terms.s1p2: The terms of purchase are not here: price, payment, delivery and returns are written in the public offer.
terms.s2p1: A handle is three letters and three digits — FLX007, say. It opens your profile at {host}/FLX007.
terms.s2p2: The handle is assigned to you the moment payment is confirmed and stays yours — it is never deleted. If the device is lost the handle is still yours: the same handle is written onto a new one.
terms.s3p1: The handle and the device are paid for once. Keeping the profile running is paid for separately: {monthly} so'm a month or {yearly} so'm a year.
terms.s3p2: The profile works without a subscription. What each plan carries is set out in full on the pricing page.
terms.s3p3: If the subscription stops, the profile returns to the standard plan. Nothing is deleted.
terms.s4title: Passing a handle to somebody else
terms.s4p1: The owner may pass a handle on at any time, from the cabinet, using the recipient's email address. On transfer the profile's contents — name, bio, links, posts, followers — are cleared and do not go to the new owner.
terms.s5p1: Some letter combinations are not sold. They get no different an answer from a handle that does not exist: the site says there is no such handle.
terms.s5p2: The list itself is not published. Printing it would hand a ready-made list to the person searching for exactly those words.
terms.s6p1: What stands on a profile is decided by its owner: name, bio, links, services and prices. The owner answers for whether they are true.
terms.s6p2: Material that breaks the law of the Republic of Uzbekistan or another person's rights may be removed from a profile.
terms.s7p1: If the terms on this page change, the date at the top of the page is updated. The text in force is the text standing on this page.

offer.metaDescription: The terms of Flex's public offer: prices, payment, delivery, returns and the seller's registered details.
offer.title: Public offer
offer.lead: This page sets out the terms of sale between {company} and the buyer. Placing an order and paying on the site counts as agreement to them. In short: the handle is yours the moment payment is confirmed and is not refundable; a device with a manufacturing fault is replaced free of charge within {days} days.
offer.authority: The original of this document is drawn up in Uzbek. The Russian and English versions are provided for convenience; in the event of a discrepancy the Uzbek text governs.
offer.s1p1: Flex is a unique handle and the profile it opens. The handle is three letters and three digits — FLX007, say — and it opens the buyer's profile at {host}/FLX007.
offer.s1p2: The handle can be carried on a physical device: an NFC card, a ring or a bracelet. The device is sold as a separate product.
offer.s2p1: A handle starts at {base} so'm and is priced automatically by how rare its letters and digits are. The formula is open: base price × letter multiplier × digit multiplier. The final sum is shown before payment.
offer.s2p2: Prices are in Uzbek so'm. Device and subscription prices are set out in full on the pages below and are sold on these same terms.
offer.s3p1: Payment goes through Payme or Click. Until it is confirmed the handle is held for {minutes} minutes and is sold to nobody else in that time. If payment does not complete, the hold is released and the handle is free again.
offer.s3p2: Companies pay by invoice and bank transfer; the document is issued in the cabinet.
offer.s4p1: The device is delivered once the order is confirmed: {tashkent} day within Tashkent, {from}–{to} days to the regions.
offer.s4p2: The handle and the profile start working as soon as payment is confirmed — there is no need to wait for the device.
offer.s5p1: A handle is not refundable. It is assigned to the buyer the moment payment completes and is sold to nobody else afterwards. That scarcity is what the handle is worth, so returning one would take from other buyers what they paid for.
offer.s5p2: If a device has a manufacturing fault — a dead NFC chip, a damaged body, a printing defect — tell us within {days} days of receiving it and we will replace it. The replacement is free.
offer.s5p3: Damage from use — scratches, breakage, water — is not a manufacturing fault.
offer.s6p1: These are given to identify the seller. There is no need to transfer money here — payment goes through Payme or Click, with the button on the site.
offer.s7p1: Questions and complaints go to the addresses on the contact page. Each is looked at within a working day.

privacy.metaDescription: What Flex collects, why it is needed, who can see it and how it is deleted.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.lead: This page explains what Flex collects, why, and who can see it. In short: the profile is a public page and what stands on it is yours to decide; everything else is the least that the service needs in order to work.
privacy.authority: The original of this document is drawn up in Uzbek. The Russian and English versions are provided for convenience; in the event of a discrepancy the Uzbek text governs.
privacy.s1p1: For the account: your phone number or email address. They are what signing in and attaching an order to you need.
privacy.s1p2: For the profile: name, bio, links, services and an image. You enter these and you change them.
privacy.s1p3: For an order: the delivery address and a contact number.
privacy.s1p4: From the business enquiry form: company name, name, phone, number of points and a note. The form sends only the fields you filled in.
privacy.s1p5: Visits to a profile are counted. On the paid plan that statistic is shown to the profile's owner.
privacy.s1p6: If you leave a contact on a profile, the name and phone you wrote are shown to the profile's owner and can be exported by them. This is kept only when you left it yourself.
privacy.s2title: A profile is a public page
privacy.s2p1: The profile a handle opens is a public, indexable page. Anybody sees everything standing on it, so put only what you want shown there.
privacy.s2p2: The phone number can be hidden, leaving only a message or Telegram button.
privacy.s3p1: What is collected is used only to provide the service: signing in, delivering an order, working out the subscription and showing the profile.
privacy.s3p2: Data is not sold and is not passed to third parties for advertising.
privacy.s4p1: To the payment systems — Payme or Click — what a payment needs in order to go through. Payment happens on their side; card details are not stored on this site.
privacy.s4p2: To the delivery service — the address and contact number needed to deliver the device.
privacy.s4p3: To the authorities, in the cases the law requires.
privacy.s5p1: The site uses two cookies: one that remembers the language you chose, and one that says you are signed in. The second is closed to scripts in the browser.
privacy.s5p2: No advertising or tracking cookies are used.
privacy.s6p1: Profile data is kept until you change or delete it. The profile can be deleted at any time.
privacy.s6p2: When a handle is passed to somebody else the profile's data is cleared and does not go to the new owner.
privacy.s6p3: Order and payment records are kept for the period the law requires.
privacy.s7p1: With a question about your data, or a request to delete it, write to the addresses on the contact page. Each is looked at within a working day.

contact.metaDescription: How to reach Flex: phone, email, the responsible person and the company's registered details.
contact.title: Contact
contact.lead: For a question, a complaint or an order — call or write. Each is looked at within a working day.
contact.replyBody: Each enquiry is looked at within a working day.
contact.addressNote: The address of registration. It is not a counter: call before coming.
contact.reqNote: These are given to identify the seller. There is no need to transfer money here — payment goes through Payme or Click, with the button on the site.
contact.businessBody: For a cafe, a hotel, a clinic or a team — fill in the form on the business page and we will come back to you.
contact.docsBody: The terms of sale are in the public offer, the rules for using the service are in the terms of use, and data is covered by the privacy policy.

login.metaDescription: We text a code to your phone — no password, no email.
login.title: Sign in with your number
login.lead: No password. Type your phone number and we'll text you a code.
login.newAccountNote: If the number is new to us, signing in opens the account.
login.phoneHint: The code arrives by SMS on this number.
login.codeHint: The code is good for 5 minutes.
login.errorPhone: That number looks incomplete. For example: +998 90 123 45 67
login.errorSend: The code didn't go out. Wait a moment and try again.
login.errorCode: That code is wrong or has expired. Ask for a new one.
login.errorServer: We can't reach the server. Wait a moment and try again.

feed.metaDescription: Posts from the numbers you follow, in one column, newest first.
feed.title: Posts
feed.lead: Everything the numbers you follow have written. Newest at the top.
feed.signedOutTitle: Sign in to read your feed
feed.signedOutBody: A feed is the posts written by the numbers you follow. That makes it a different page for every reader, and until we know who you are there is nothing to show. Sign in and the feed becomes yours.
feed.downTitle: We could not open the feed just now
feed.downBody: The server did not answer. That does not mean the numbers you follow have written nothing. Refresh the page in a little while.
feed.emptyBody: The numbers you follow have not posted anything. Find a few more in the residents list.

catalogue.metaDescription: Every design a Flex card can be ordered in. Whichever you pick, it is one number and one profile.
catalogue.title: Card designs
catalogue.lead: What your card can look like. The number stays the same — the design is yours to choose.
catalogue.note: Every card is printed with the number of the person who ordered it. All ten here carry the same sample, {handle}, so you are comparing designs rather than numbers.

designs.genesis: The standard card. Deep black, a grain in the surface and one lime dot — the FLEX CARD series itself.
designs.lime: The inversion: a solid lime field with black type. Read from across a room.
designs.grid: A dot grid. Dry and exact, the way an engineering drawing is.
designs.sheen: A diagonal run of light — turned in the hand it catches like metal.
designs.naqsh: An eight-pointed lattice. Our own drawing, built from the geometry of traditional tilework.
designs.paper: White, and nearly empty. The number and a hairline edge.
designs.rahbar: Absolute black, crossed by one polished silver line. Shows the least and says the most.
designs.devops: A low-contrast circuit trace on black, with a single track lit in lime. Technical without being loud.
designs.suzani: A suzani medallion on deep indigo — the texture of embroidery, a shade lighter than its ground, with one gold thread.
designs.xarita: Gold engraving on black: the map of Uzbekistan with a Humo medallion beside it. Not a state emblem — our own drawing.

catalogue.ctaTitle: The design is the last thing you choose
catalogue.ctaBody: The number comes first. Which design gets printed on the card is decided at order time, and it can be changed later.

empty.title: No number yet
empty.body: Pick three letters and three digits — it stays yours for life. Once payment clears, the number shows up here.

home.waiting: {count, plural, one {# person asking to follow} other {# people asking to follow}}
home.endingSoon: Premium ends in {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}

profile.title: Profile
profile.hint: Name, role, links, services — everything a stranger reads.

posts.title: Posts
posts.hint: Shown on your profile and in followers' feeds.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.hint: Who sees the profile, and who is asking in.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.hint: How often it was opened, from where, what got pressed.

theme.title: Design
theme.hint: The look the profile opens in.

qr.title: QR code
qr.hint: For phones without NFC and for print.

leads.title: Contacts
leads.hint: Contacts left by visitors on your profile.
leads.emptyHint: When visitors exchange their business card on your profile, they appear here.

transfer.title: Transfer
transfer.hint: Transfer number ownership to another person.
transfer.sendHint: Enter the recipient's phone number. Until accepted, the number remains yours.

plan.title: Plan
plan.hint: What is paid for and when it ends.

profile.name: Name
profile.bioHint: Up to 280 characters. The line or two you say when you meet someone.
profile.tagsHint: Comma-separated, up to 5: design, IT, marketing
profile.pictureHint: The address of an uploaded file. Uploading is done in the app for now.

error.server: Not saved. Try again in a moment.

payment.label: Payment link
payment.hint: Your personal Payme or Click link. The profile shows a “Pay” button.

booking.label: Booking
booking.hint: Where people book you — Calendly, a bot, a site.

privacy.closedHint: A stranger sees only the picture, the name and the number. The rest opens once you say yes.
privacy.commentsHint: Strangers can leave comments on your profile.
privacy.nobodyWaiting: Nobody is waiting right now. When someone asks to follow, they show up here.
privacy.openNobodyWaits: The profile is open — following needs no permission. Close it with the switch above and requests land here.

error.tooMany: Too many posts in an hour. Try again later.

posts.afterPayment: You can post once payment has cleared.
posts.deleteBody: It disappears from the profile and from followers' feeds. This cannot be undone.

stats.premiumDaily: A daily chart — which day, how many times
stats.premiumSources: Where they came from — card, QR or link

plan.title: Plan
plan.freeLead: The profile is open and the basics work
plan.daysLeft: {days, plural, one {# day left} other {# days left}}

lapse.opens: The profile keeps opening — a tap on the card shows the same page.
lapse.stats: Statistics show totals only: days, links and sources close.
lapse.keeps: The number stays yours and nothing is deleted. The day payment resumes, everything is back.

seo.ogLead: A unique number, an NFC card and a profile. No app needed.
